Fusebox does less work when serving cached embeddings, preparing Claude requests, querying usage, syncing history and rendering the dashboard. Model discovery now shares a bounded scheduler, with accurate messages when checks overlap.

## Changes

- **Embeddings cache.** Warm hits no longer scan the entire cache. Expiry sweeps run when needed, and byte accounting is maintained incrementally while preserving TTL, capacity and eviction behavior.
- **Claude request preparation.** Billing fingerprints inspect only the required UTF-16 characters instead of allocating a vector for the whole prompt. Prompt text is borrowed and replaced system blocks are moved instead of cloned, preserving the outgoing content.
- **Model discovery.** Manual and automatic checks share four slots and suppress duplicate requests for the same account. Recently checked or already-running accounts skip the queue promptly. The dashboard distinguishes checks still in progress from accounts checked recently, including in Chinese. Cancelled manual batches leave queued accounts due for the next automatic poll.
- **Usage storage and collectors.** Large breakdowns select the returned groups before serializing JSON. Compression batches reuse a scratch buffer and retain right-sized blobs. Collectors size each observation once instead of repeatedly cloning and serializing the growing batch, preserving the exact upload cutoff and payload.
- **Dashboard.** Date formatters are reused across chart hovers, and model-family coverage is aggregated in one pass. Existing time-zone, ordering and coverage behavior is preserved.

## Upgrading

- From v0.11.0, the usage database remains on schema 5, with no migration or new settings.
- Model refreshes with more than four eligible accounts run four at a time and can take longer than the previous unlimited fan-out. Overlapping checks report their pending status and deliver results through the existing live updates.
- The model-check API adds an `in_progress` count alongside `asked` and `new`.

Validation passed 759 Rust, 144 dashboard and 46 Python tests, plus release restart/rollback checks and 12 collector acceptance checks. Component measurements and their limits are documented in the [optimization report](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/blob/v0.11.1/docs/optimization-followup-2026-10-29.md); they do not measure provider latency or whole-request speedups.

[Full comparison with v0.11.0](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/compare/v0.11.0...v0.11.1).
